Each reads instead the registry declarations the summary's `Name` role is itself derived from, never a command's spelling: the Eval trait from `EVALUATES_CODE` and `DEFERS_BODY` on a call's `Body` words, with every word after the first where the script concatenates its arguments (`SCRIPT_CONCATENATES_ARGS`), and from `PERFORMS_SUBSTITUTION` on its words; `upvar`'s pairs and level from the head's frame-effect declaration, the level word present by argument-count parity and its value a `FrameLevel` (`FrameEffectSpec::resolve_in`, the type `ParamRole::Name` carries), and `namespace upvar`'s pairs from the words after the namespace word of a scope alias that names one; `global` and `variable` from their scope-alias plan (`CommandRegistry::alias_frame`, `Global` or `Namespace`) with their `VarWrite` operands, and a scope-alias declaration (`var_scoping::is_scope_alias_call`, over `CREATES_SCOPE_ALIAS`) as a link that writes nothing; both copy trackers from the `VarWrite` role of the word written, the copy made by a cell write of its value word (`ResolvedSemantics::writes_value_word`) and ended by any other write; a loop's list from `LOOP_LIST_HEADER` and the word after each `LoopVarList` word, its body and condition from the `Body` and `Expr` roles the role scan already reads; `after`'s script from its `Body` role, its subcommand resolution keeping `cancel` and `info` out; and slot resolution's frame and trace arms from `INTROSPECTS_BY_NAME`, `CURRENT_FRAME_INTROSPECTION` and `TARGETS_VARIABLE_BY_NAME` with the `VarWrite` and `CommandName` roles. The plan's "reads the summary" is met as "reads the declarations the summary is derived from" at those sites; its contract points stand — the four files in `CLEAN_FILES`, no consumer matching a command by name, one fact one owner — and every existing `param_traits` test is byte-identical.

Taken in the review fixes of slice 13 (§ *Slice 13* › *Record (2026-10-07): review fixes for slice 13*):

- **D308 — A run that reads how a procedure completes takes a certain raise as the end of its path, in every block** (B1; the coordinator's ruling, departing from its words where D222 holds the unit's lattice). The ruling has a call that cannot complete be a certain raise in the caller's lattice, `DefValues::Raised` with `keep_prior`, and the exit reading take a statement the lattice knows raises as ending the path. Measured, the call was not what reported `completes: false`: `bump`'s re-run under `v` = `foo` reached its exit, since its `incr` route's proven error widened outside a handler, as D222 has every error do, so the re-run completed and `[c]` folded to 0. So the raise is taken where exits are read: a run made to read how a procedure completes — a callee's re-run, a summary's own run, the seedless return run and O103's argument-sensitive re-run (`ModuleRun::reads_exits`) — answers `DefValues::Raised` for a route's proven error, a word's, an expression's and a definition-less statement probed for one, in every block, as a run does where a handler is thrown to, and for a call to a procedure of the module that never completes normally: a word count its parameters reject, a summary that never completes, a re-run under the call's seeds that reaches no exit (`never_completes`, `procedure_raises`). The solver's `Raised` handling is unchanged: the statement's places keep what they held, the rest of the block keeps its prior values and the block opens no normal edge. A unit's lattice keeps D222 — a raise there proves no code unreachable and gives no diagnostic a reason — so there such a call's places wait, as a callee that never completes left them. The exit reading (`exit_value`, a re-run's normal exits) reads no value where the run holds a statement that certainly raises where no handler takes the throw (`RunCompletion::raises`): a raise beside an exit means some call of the procedure raises, and a fold answers for every call it rewrites, so the reading is stricter than "the path ends there", which would fold `[c 1]` to the other path's value where `c` raises for 1.
- **D309 — A call whose completion no re-run decided leaves the exit reading no value, on both O103 paths** (B1; the ruling's "a call whose completion the re-run cannot decide", made definite). A call's completion is decided where a re-run of the callee was made under exact seeds — every parameter's value, and each place either unbound or bound to a known value — and that run held no raise beside its exits and no undecided call of its own (`Rerun::decided`). It is undecided where no re-run was made (the depth and count bounds, a recursion its seeds do not end, a callee the summary does not answer, a call in an effect-free word below `ModuleLevel::Results`), or where the seeds were not exact: `proc c {x} {set n $x; bump n; return 0}` has no seedless constant, and `[c 1]` folds to 0 on the argument-sensitive path while `[c foo]` does not. The ruling names the seedless path; the rule is the run's, so a call inside the argument-sensitive re-run whose seeds that run does not hold exactly is undecided there too. What stays open is #2390's (the record's *#2390, measured*): a call that names none of the caller's variables is answered without a re-run, as before, so its completion is not read, and a statement that may raise under the run's seeds is not one the run proves raises.
- **D310 — Where a run holds no existence rung, a procedure's entry version of a place is bound for a parameter and unbound otherwise** (B1). The seedless and O103 runs hold no existence rung (D290), so the place `bump n` names at its entry version had no fact, its seed was not exact, and `proc c {} {bump n; return 0}` stopped folding `[c]` to 0 from 8.5, where the cell is created and the fold is right. Those runs read only pure procedures, whose `Name` arguments name plain locals (D305): unset at entry unless a parameter.
- **D311 — A `Name` parameter the call omits names the place its default spells** (B2, at the coordinator's ruling; closes #2416). `call_transfer` takes the default the parameter list declares, as Tcl decodes it, as the call's place, and the CFG builder's call-by-name definitions take it from `UpvarInfo::param_defaults`, so the place has a definition at the call and the summary applies there; a default that names no variable the analysis can place — an element, a name with a substitution character, or a parameter list the strict parse rejects — widens the caller's frame as a computed argument does (`OmittedName`). The purity scan still finds no own place for an omitted argument, so its caller stays impure and O103 does not fold it; its lattice proves the value, and O126 no longer deletes the store the call reads. The read half follows the same rule: the call-by-name reads W220 and W211 leave alone (`collect_call_by_name_reads`) take an omitted parameter's default from `ProcSummary::param_defaults`, since the new definition alone made `set n 1; bumpd; return $n` report W220, which the base did not; it also ends the W211 the base reported on `set n 1; bumpd; return 0`, the same omission (#2416's), where tclsh 8.4 to 9.1 read the store through the alias (`n` is 2 after the call). The per-procedure optimiser of `tcl-lsp-db` keeps its own callee projection without defaults: its O109 and O126 read the CFG builder's `alias_observed_vars`, which carry the default through the shared upvar context, so its rewrites do not move. One reach of the barrier the corpus shows: an empty default, the idiom for "no variable" (`proc VerifyRules {rules {canonvar {}}} {…}` called as `VerifyRules $rules`), is not a name the analysis can place, so the call widens its caller's frame, and over the 1120-file corpus that silences one W210, `canon` at `pt/pt_pegrammar.tcl:78`, which the base reported where the `catch` before it returns on error; an explicit `{}` word names nothing and widens nothing, so the omitted and the written argument differ there. Reading the default as the literal word the call would write is the refinement, left for the coordinator.
- **D312 — A `Name` argument that is not the name it normalises to is a barrier** (found beside B2, the slice's own). `call_transfer` normalised the word before testing it for an element, and normalising drops the index, so `bump a(k)` named `a` and stated it bound as a scalar: `[array exists a]` decided false (I230, O101), where tclsh 8.4 to 9.1 return `arr`. The base binary left the program alone.
- **D313 — A `Name` argument that names a place outside the caller's frame is a write of the caller's summary** (S1, at the coordinator's ruling). `component_outer_writes` (`interprocedural/transfer.rs`) states among a procedure's `globals` the places its calls' `Name` arguments name outside its frame (`outer_arguments`): a qualified word (`bump ::g`; a relative qualified word names its namespace's place or the global namespace's, as `outer_places` reads a qualified write), and a local the procedure links to a namespace's variable, read from the registry's scope-alias declarations (`linked_locals`, over `alias_facts`: `upvar #0`, `global`, `variable`, `namespace upvar`), passed as the argument (`upvar #0 g x; bump x`, `global g; bump g`) — an omitted argument's default among them (D311). The place takes the callee's outcomes on it where every normal completion makes the call with the argument naming it — a statement of the entry block, after the one link the argument reads — no other call names it, nothing else the procedure runs writes it and nothing it runs destroys a variable, in a set of one procedure; otherwise it is may-bound, and may-unbound too where a body the procedure runs destroys a variable or a callee may unbind such a place (`proc s {c} {if {$c} {reset ::q}}` states `::q` unbinds then may bind; `proc r {} {reset ::q}` states it unbinds). The places a callee's summary states are the caller's too: `GlobalWriteInfo`, which the summary read alone, carries no write made through a callee's link (#2410). A procedure whose `Name` argument is a local linked to a place the summary cannot name — at a computed level or namespace, to two places, to an object's or a connection's variable — has no summary, nor has a caller of it (D299), and the Explorer's `transfer` line reads `none — a call is a barrier`. So `keeps_to_its_frame` answers false for the review's `c`, `d` and `e`, and `tcl explore --show interproc` prints `globals: ::g binds a scalar` for each; the top level's `g` after a call to `c` is still #2410's.
- **D314 — W210 reads the step a call's summary states for the place a `Name` argument names** (S2, at the coordinator's ruling). `build_phi_undef_index` (`analyser/diagnostics/helpers.rs`) takes each definition a call to a procedure of the module gives a place a `Name` argument names with the step the callee's summary states for it (`call_steps`, over `value_transfer::summary_steps`, which resolves the call as the shared lattice does and reads `ModuleProcedures::call_transfer`): a step that leaves the place unset whatever it held — an unbind — kills the definition, so a read of it is read before set, as after `unset`; a step that sets it is a definition, as before; and any other — a may-bind, a preserve, or the step that may unset whatever the place held, which a summary also states where its body links the place other than cleanly (`ANY_OUTCOME`) — reads the version before the call, as an opaque `switch`'s arm definition does, so a read after it is read before set where nothing set the place before the call. A may-unset of a place set before draws nothing: the summary does not say whether the unset is the body's or the analysis's caution, and `proc f {name c} {if {$c} {upvar 1 $name v; set v 1}}` — a link in a branch — states it. A call the summary does not answer — a callee with no summary, an argument that substitutes or names an element, a word count the callee rejects — stays the assignment of every place its definitions name. W210 has one wording, so a may-bind draws the plain finding (`Variable 'k' is read before it is set`): the review's w01, w03, w04, w05 and w07 report, d01 (`bump q; puts $q`) and w06 (`set k 1; maybe k $c; puts $k`) stay silent. W211 is unchanged: a `Name` argument is a read of its place (`collect_call_by_name_reads`), whatever the step. One reach the rule has that a body's own loop does not: a may-bind a summary states for a write inside a loop that may run no pass draws the finding — `proc fill {name xs} {upvar 1 $name v; foreach x $xs {set v $x}}; proc p {xs} {fill r $xs; puts $r}` reports `r`, which tclsh raises on for `p {}` — where the same loop written in `p` does not, W210 taking a loop the function writes as running (`loop_entry_only_undef`); the summary's outcome does not say why the bind may not happen. Over the corpus — every `.tcl` file of tcllib 2.0's modules and of `samples/` and `editors/vscode/`, 1120 files, `tcl diag` and `tcl opt --profile full` each — the second commit's binary draws no new W210 and moves no rewrite against the landing's.

Taken in slice 7, broader execution and runtime consumers (§ *Slice 7* › *Record (2026-10-07): slice 7* has the witnesses):

- **D315 — The tcllib, Tk and standard-library specs stay Rust spec modules** (the coordinator's ruling 1, at the repository owner's direction of 7 October 2026). B-CC7 — VT7.5 "follows the move of the tcllib specs to SpecTcl" — is void, and its entry says so; the `KNOWN_GAPS` reasons that cited the move now cite this decision. VT7.5 is delivered in the Rust form: per candidate of the evaluation page's Tier 2 list and every tcllib row in `KNOWN_GAPS`, a registry-owned direct route over a `tcl-cmd-core` core proven against tcllib 2.0 under tclsh 8.5.19 to 9.1.0, or a declared implementation the Rust spec module carries, its body tcllib 2.0's own procedure pinned by content hash; a candidate the host platform or the clock decides declares `none (platform)`, one the routes cannot model `none (form-unsupported)`, and what one checkpoint cannot prove stays `none (unauthored)` with its name in the hand-back. No spec moves out of Rust.
- **D316 — The grapheme cursor rows are slice 7's** (ruling 2): routed over a shared core where the grapheme-cluster tables `tcl-cmd-core` or the runtime carry suffice for one, `none (unauthored)` otherwise.
- **D317 — The lane document and its README entry stay until the coordinator's final scrub** (ruling 3): the landing updates the design pages' status lines and this record only, and its commit message is the plan's without its last sentence.
- **D318 — Every slice 7 item runs under opus** (ruling 4), the plan's sonnet items included.
- **D319 — The upstream starting point stands** (ruling 5): HEAD is two commits behind `origin/rust` (#2377, #2380), neither touching the slice's files; the merge is the coordinator's, after the slice.
- **D320 — VT7.11 binds the consumer-contracts lane's step 10 seam** (ruling 6; that lane's D10.56 and D10.57): `HostKind::WasmExtension` (`wasm_extension`), the artefact hash in `ImplementationIdentity.content_hash`, the loader's `extension FILE PREFIX` row, production evaluation declining `Transient` with no WASM extension host installed, and a language server that never links wasmtime.
- **D321 — An index reads as its release reads it** (a defect found in passing, fixed in its own commit ahead of the first checkpoint because the list cell updates would have widened it). The shared index parser read every release with one lenient grammar, so under tcl8.4 and f5-irules the optimiser folded `string range abcdef 0 1+1` to `abc`, and `lindex {a b c} 1+1`, `lrange {a b c d} 0 end+1` and `string index abc 0+1` with it, where tclsh 8.4.20 raises `bad index "1+1": must be integer or end?-integer?`. `index::parse` reads the grammar of the release it is given, measured on tclsh 8.4.20 to 9.1.0 (`each_release_reads_an_index_as_its_tclsh_does`): 8.4 an integer or `end-N` and `end`'s abbreviations; 8.5 and 8.6 also `end+N` and the sums, `N` starting at once; 9.0 on without the abbreviations. A caller naming no release answers where every release agrees, so the release-blind `lindex`, `lrange` and `string` folds lose index arithmetic (precision-limitations.md has the entry).
- **D322 — An iRules pure function answers only what F5's reference states** (VT7.1). TMM's commands have no runtime here, so the only evidence for a core is the published reference (`clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/`) and the standards it names; a core answers the behaviour the reference states or shows in an example and is `Unmodelled` for every input outside it — a search string or field that is not there, a `substr` count of 0 (the reference notes it does not work in 11.5.4 and 11.6.0), a URI with a fragment, a `%` escape, user information or a dot segment, a `URI::port` scheme with no default the reference lists (it shows `myproto` as 0, which says nothing of other schemes), prefixes on both `IP::addr` operands. The route declines such an input as unsupported, and the simulator answers it with the generated stub it always had.
- **D323 — A byte function reads ASCII words alone** (VT7.1). `b64encode`, `b64decode`, `crc32` and the digests take bytes, and TMM's conversion of a value to bytes is not stated; every conversion it might make reads an ASCII word as its bytes, so the cores take only those, and a digest's or `b64decode`'s bytes are a byte array in the lattice (characters U+0000 to U+00FF, `Constructed(ByteArray)`). `crc32` is sign-extended from 32 bits, as the reference states; `b64decode` answers only canonical base64, every text `b64encode` gives, since TMM raises `conversion error` on text it cannot decode and the reference does not say which.
- **D324 — `htonl`, `htons`, `ntohl` and `ntohs` declare `none (platform)`, with no core** (VT7.1; a departure from the plan's core list). The answer is the host's byte order — `htonl 1` is 16777216 on a little-endian host and 1 on a big-endian one — and the reference states no result; `NoRouteSemantics`, the smallest declaration of a pure command with no route and its reason (`value_transfer/builtins.rs`), says so in the inventory.
- **D325 — `URI::escape` has no route** (VT7.1; a departure from the plan's list). The reference has no page for it; the spec's `URI::encode` alias is the spec's own claim, not published behaviour, so nothing is proven to model.
- **D326 — `URI::encode` answers only the characters the reference's example shows** (VT7.1). The two editions of its page differ on `[` and `]` (`%5b` and `%5d` in one, absent in the other), and the treatment of every character the example does not show is not stated: letters, digits, `(`, `)` and `*` stand, space, `&`, `@` and `#` escape as `%20`, `%26`, `%40` and `%23`, and any other character is unmodelled.
- **D327 — The simulator registers the cores in front of the unchanged stub table** (VT7.1; a departure from the plan's file list). `LiveSession` registers each core as a host command under the mock name `register_all` looks for (`rust/tcl-irule-test/src/pure_functions.rs`), so it takes the stub's place, and an input the core does not model falls back to that stub through the same table. `_mock_stubs.tcl` and `gen_irule_test_data.rs` are unchanged: the runner on a real `tclsh` cannot load a Rust core and keeps the stubs, and `cargo xtask gen-irule-test-data --check` passes.
- **D328 — `ledit` exists from 9.0** (VT7.2; the plan says 9.1). tclsh 9.0.4 has it (`ledit l 1 1 X Y` over `a b c` is `a X Y c`), and the tree's spec says `TCL90_PLUS`.
- **D329 — The list cell updates run under the release, in the lattice and in both runtimes** (VT7.2). Each core takes a `TclVersion`: the index grammar, the append at an index equal to a level's length (from 8.6) and the error wording are the release's. The route answers under a profile that names a release, and with none only where every release computes the same answer; the VM's `lset` builtin and its compiled `LSET_LIST` and `LSET_FLAT`, and the WASM runtime's `lset`, `ledit` and `lpop`, call the same cores under the release they emulate — so the VM under 8.4 and 8.5 raises where it appended, reads 8.4's index grammar, and the runtime's `lpop` now takes a nested index path, which it refused.
- **D330 — A store whose value is a call to a pure procedure of the module that provably completes for any accepted arguments cannot raise** (the coordinator's ruling, refining D253; the completion-proof fix, landed between slice 7's checkpoints — § *Slice 7* › *Record (2026-10-07): slice 7* has its row). D253 keeps a store whose value runs a command substitution unless the lattice folds it cleanly, a call to a procedure being no clean fold, pure or not, since purity says the call changes nothing, not that it completes; a unit's lattice takes no call's result (D304), so the unused call of a pure wrapper stayed, `set a [label abc]` over `string length` among them, which cannot raise. The summary now states completion apart (`ProcSummary::completes`): a procedure completes where its body is straight-line — `set` of its own plain scalars, calls and a simple `return` — reads only its parameters and scalars it set, and runs only commands that complete whatever their words hold: a registry command the module trusts and the document does not declare, whose resolved invocation declares the normal completion alone (`Exact([Ok])`) under a word count its arity accepts, or a procedure of the module, resolved as Tcl resolves a command under a binding that stands, called with a word count its parameters accept, that completes in turn. It is a least fixpoint, so a recursion, which the nesting limit ends, never completes; for a call that does not recurse the limit is set aside, as every fold sets it aside. The raise proof (`RaiseProof::calls_complete`) takes an `AssignValue` whose every command substitution calls a pure procedure that completes — resolved from the function's namespace, with an accepted word count, under a binding no redefinition, `rename` or alias moves, in a module that traces no command — its words literal or variable reads the existence rung holds set, as a value that cannot raise, so O126, O109 and O108 may delete its store. A stub states purity, not completion (`-pure` is `Traits::PURE`, which `lindex` carries and raises beside), so the store of a wrapper over one stays; the summary built from the IR alone, which holds no command trust, states no completion. A direct registry call, `set a [string length $y]` with `y` set, stays on the clean-fold path: deciding it would need the document's declarations in the elimination pass and in the per-procedure memo's key. Only `string length` declares an ok-only completion today; a registry command gains the proof by declaring its completion.
- **D331 — The path routes answer only where the POSIX and Windows readings agree** (the coordinator's ruling on VT7.3, option (a), applied in the second checkpoint). The plan has the `file` path routes decline under `Needs::PLATFORM` where the profile does not fix the platform; the evaluation page's contract that `PLATFORM` is never satisfiable on the direct route stands, and no profile fixes a platform today, so read literally the routes would never answer and `auto_path_eval.rs` would lose every fold it makes. `file join`, `dirname`, `tail`, `extension`, `rootname` and `split` answer where the POSIX and Windows readings agree — no backslash, no drive, UNC or volume-relative root, no `~` — and decline `ReleaseAmbiguous(Platform)` otherwise; `file normalize` declares `none (platform)`; `auto_path_eval.rs` reads the routes for those forms and keeps its own host-path arithmetic for the rest, as the language server's host resolution, waived as `irreducible`, so it enters `CLEAN_FILES` with waivers rather than at zero sites. precision-limitations.md records the forms a platform axis a caller could fix (the language server's host, or a profile pinning a target platform) would answer, assigned to no slice.
- **D332 — A file name's parts read as tclsh reads them** (a defect from before the slice, fixed in its own commit ahead of the second checkpoint because VT7.3's path routes run the same cores). `tcl_cmd_core::path`, which both runtimes' `file dirname`, `tail`, `extension` and `rootname` call, took the extension from the tail's last dot after its first byte and the directory from the text before the last separator, so `file extension .bashrc` gave the empty string and `file dirname a//b` gave `a/`, where tclsh 8.4.20 to 9.1.0 give `.bashrc` and `a`: 21 of the 192 answers measured over 48 names differed. The cores now read a name as `tclFileName.c` does on Unix. Its elements are the root `/` where it starts with a separator and the non-empty runs between separators (`split`, new); `dirname` and `tail` are the elements but the last and the last, as `TclPathPart` takes them, so a root alone has no tail and a relative name of one element has the directory `.`; `extension` is `TclGetExtension`'s, from the last dot to the end where no separator follows it, so `.bashrc` is all extension and `a/b.c/` has none; and `join` (new) is the elements after the last absolute name. Every release reads these alike except a leading `//`, which 9.0 keeps as a root of its own, and an element starting with `~`, a home directory to 8.x and a name to 9.0: the cores keep the readings the runtimes had, 8.x's and 9.0's, and the path routes take neither form.
- **D333 — `split` splits on tclsh's four separators by default** (a defect from before the slice, fixed in its own commit ahead of the second checkpoint because VT7.4's `split` route runs the same core). `tcl_cmd_core::list::split`, which both runtimes' `split` calls, took its default separators from the six-character whitespace set `concat` trims (`TCL_WS`, with the vertical tab and the form feed), so `split "a\vb\fc d"` gave four elements where tclsh 8.4.20 to 9.1.0 give two: `Tcl_SplitObjCmd` splits on `" \n\t\r"`. The default is now that set (`SPLIT_WS`).

### Open questions for the owner

Each with the assumption the plan proceeds on.

- **Q1 — The three nested budgets.** The evaluation page lands them in
  slice 2; the hand-off deferred them. *Assumption*: slice 4 (D3).
- **Q2 — `command_substitution_is_none` "flips".** Its program, `[clock
  seconds] + 1`, reads the wall clock and can never fold. *Assumption*:
  slice 9 renames it `command_substitution_evaluates_through_the_nested_service`
  over `[incr x] + 1` and keeps the clock program as its negative case.
- **Q3 — #2143's W123 half.** The analyser's W123 pass runs over the
  source walk, which never sees `specialise_factories`' children; the
  template-word plan gives the child its span, not its registration.
  *Assumption*: slice 5 fixes the span half and its landing says "Pins the
  span half of #2143"; if the owner assigns the W123 half here, VT5.9
  grows a bridge carrying the unit's materialised procedures to the
  walk's W123 pass, and the landing says "Closes #2143".
- **Q4 — `ActivationStore`.** The page's mechanism cannot write the
  calling frame through `HostCommand`. *Assumption*:
  `Engine::confine_stores` (D10), an engine capability the page did not
  consider; the page's § *Per-evaluation state* is amended in VT4.15.
- **Q5 — The `Set` hook's `interp create` binding.** It is the
  interpreter-domain axis, not the value axis. *Assumption*: it moves with
  the hook in VT8.9, reached from the generic binding and keyed by the
  value word's resolved `interp create`.
- **Q6 — The shared lattice's stance on an unbounded binding transition.**
  Upstream's `ObservedBindings` keeps folding when one unresolved head
  raises the `dynamic` top, while the interface page's decline table reads
  "binding validity: … renamed, aliased, redefined, or in an opaque
  namespace". *Assumption*: the plan adopts upstream's two stances (D21),
  because every rewrite re-proves under `WholeModule`.
- **Q7 — Reclassified gap rows.** `const` to slice 8 and `lset`, `ledit`,
  `lpop` to slice 7 (D4, D5). *Assumption*: accepted.
- **Q8 — The regexp runtime delta.** *Assumption*: accepted (D18).
- **Q9 — #2214 in this lane.** *Assumption*: VT2.9 fixes it unless a
  `rust` pull request closes it first.
- **Q10 — Slice 5's size.** Twenty items in one slice. *Assumption*: one
  slice, six checkpoints, one landing, as the plan defines it.
- **Q11 — The diagnostic-policy lane's three questions to the
  `tcl-compiler` owner** (the file-directive fold, W305's self-filter, a
  single-bucket `line_suppressed`). *Assumption*: they are not this lane's;
  it neither answers nor blocks them.
- **Q12 — The evaluator generation in salsa** (D98). The per-procedure
  lattice key carries the building worker's generation, but the unit query
  above it is memoised on its inputs alone. *Assumption*: the server sets
  a salsa input for the generation when a worker's host changes, in a
  later slice or the consumer-contracts lane; until then a transient
  decline served to a healthy worker is imprecise, never wrong.
  **Answered on 2026-09-23 (D104)**, in this slice once the
  diagnostic-policy lane had freed `rust/tcl-lsp-server`: the evaluator
  epoch is a salsa input the server sets where it reloads packs and after
  each diagnostics pass.
- **Q13 — An exhausted request re-declines what it paid for** (D100).
  *Assumption*: the evaluation page's rule stands as built — a pass gets a
  tenth of what is left, and a re-evaluated statement the pass cannot pay
  for declines — and charging a pass only for work an earlier pass did not
  already pay for is the refinement if the degradation shows up in
  practice.
  **Accepted on 2026-09-23**, as built and with no change: sound, since a
  re-decline publishes `Overdefined` and never a stale constant. The
  precision it costs is per function: once one run's evaluations spend
  its request (`Budget::request()`, 50,000,000 units; D99 says what they
  bound on each route), every route-evaluated definition a later
  sweep re-evaluates declines with `declined: budget: Request` and ends
  `Overdefined`, the ones earlier sweeps folded included, so the function
  keeps none of its route folds rather than those made before the point
  of exhaustion (D100's measurement: all twelve `string length` folds of
  one procedure under a 500-unit request). What reads those constants — a
  constant condition (I230), a forwarded value (O100) — sees none for
  them. Only a function whose route evaluations together cost more than
  the request pays it; the refinement above stays the answer if that
  shows up in practice.

### Deltas flagged for the owner

- **F1 — Folding under a profile that names no release.** The hand-off's
  per-operation admission makes `incr x 5`, `append`, `lappend`, `string
  range` and every later direct route fold under every vendor dialect
  (iRules included) where each modelled release agrees, while the
  evaluation page's `admit` step 2 reads "a bit whose field is `None` is a
  decline". The page's per-axis rules support the reading; its literal
  step does not. CC9.2 later gives iRules a measured base (B-CC8).
  **Closed — the owner ruled on 2026-09-22:** "What's the most accurate
  thing to do with folding, that's the right answer." Unanimity decides: a
  route folds where its answer is proven identical under every release the
  profile can denote, any per-axis disagreement declines with
  `ReleaseAmbiguous(Axis)`, and a dialect that declares a base release
  (iRules on its 8.4-derived engine) evaluates under it, a vendor pack that
  diverges on an axis blocking the fold by declaring the axis. The
  per-operation admission stands as built; `value-evaluation.md`'s `admit`
  steps 1 and 2 and § *Target semantics* now say so, and
  `value-transfers.md` § *Rulings* 7 and 8 record it. The base-release half
  is built by VT4.1 (D72): `TargetSemantics::of` reads the profile's
  declared runtime (`DialectProfile::runtime_version`), so iRules evaluates
  under 8.4, and `TclVersion::from_profile` (CC9.2's) is untouched.
- **F2 — The budget deferral** (D3, Q1): a scope move, not a behaviour.
- **F3 — The inventory committed from a failing gate run** at the
  checkpoint: a process deviation, corrected by VT2.0.
- **F4 — The `ObservedBindings` stance** (D21, Q6): the shared lattice
  folds under an unbounded binding transition that the rewrite stance
  refuses.

No other delta in this plan lacks a mandate; each slice's table cites
its own.
